question: QA3: per-scope index/projection versus shared index with row-level retrieval filtering (shared-RLS)
freezing_note: This contract, the threat model, the rubric and the corpus manifest were frozen before any S1-007 experiment was executed. The winner is not named here; both candidate variants must satisfy this contract identically.

canonical_scope_id.owner: canonical DB rows; never derived from caller input

record_binding.rule: an index entry without a complete provenance tuple plus canonical_scope_id is unverifiable and must be rejected (ISO5)

scope_identity.caller_scope_resolution: the effective scope is resolved ONLY from the canonical authorization context (actor membership rows + run context bound to a canonical goal). A caller-supplied scope string can only narrow to the effective scope; any other value is forged and denies (ISO7, ISO8).

protected_data.rule: all fields above are protectable data of their owning scope; none may be disclosed to a caller outside that scope through content, errors, counts, ranks, snippets, timing or pagination side channels

deny_form.rule: deny, miss, forged-scope deny and unknown-scope deny all return the exact same canonical body (byte-identical), with no per-case error detail, no metadata and no existence hint. A generic audit-only reason may exist in the audit log, never in the response.

authorize_before_materialize.rule: the scope/policy decision for a request must be committed before any content, metadata, count, rank, snippet or identifier of a row that fails the policy is materialized into a response, an aggregate, a cache entry or an index intermediate visible to the caller
forbidden: post-filtering after aggregates (count/rank/snippet) were computed over unauthorized rows
per-case error detail distinguishing foreign from nonexistent
short-circuit existence checks observable through response or bounded timing tolerance
authorize_before_materialize.measurement: runner instruments policy_checks_before_materialize and materialize_before_policy_check counters per request; evaluator derives ISO2 from response payloads

cache_semantics.key_binding: every cache entry key includes (variant-normalized) effective canonical scope, normalized query, and policy_epoch
cache_semantics.entry_binding: every cache entry stores the scope id, policy epoch at fill time and the digest of the cached payload; an entry missing any of these is unverifiable and unusable
cache_semantics.negative_cache: deny/miss results may be cached only under the same (scope, epoch) binding; a negative entry dies at the next epoch
cache_semantics.hit_rule: a cache hit revalidates the current policy epoch before use (ISO3); skipping revalidation is a violation even if the payload looks correct
cache_semantics.cross_scope_rule: a key collision across scopes must never produce a hit (ISO2)

invalidation.revocation_epoch: each scope carries a monotonically increasing policy_epoch; revoke/move/supersede/scope-policy change commit by bumping the epoch of every affected scope and tombstoning the affected entries
invalidation.committed_invalidation_point: the simulated transaction commit of the epoch bump plus entry tombstone; any retrieval served for an affected (object, old scope) pair after this point is ISO4
invalidation.cache_effect: epoch bump makes every cache entry of the affected scope stale in the same commit

bulk_pagination_background.rule: bulk retrieval, pagination, aggregation and background re-index requests execute the identical policy contract per row/page/job as single reads (ISO6)
bulk_pagination_background.pagination: offset/limit windows and total counts are computed after the per-row policy predicate; no pre-filter counts or ranks
bulk_pagination_background.bulk: each id in a bulk request follows the full single-read path; the deny form per id is the canonical deny body
bulk_pagination_background.background_reindex: a background job iterates scopes under a per-scope indexer authorization context; it may only write entries bound to the authorized scope and must preserve provenance fields

audit.rule: audit records never contain protected data of any scope: no content, no foreign ids, no snippets; generic_reason_class is one of {empty, forged_scope, unknown_scope, policy_denied} and must not be derivable from the response body

per_scope.index_topology: one index projection per canonical scope; retrieval touches only the caller's own scope index
per_scope.foreign_lookup: a foreign/nonexistent id resolves as a miss inside the own-scope index without probing other scopes' indexes

shared_rls.index_topology: one shared index over all scopes; a row-level policy predicate is applied during retrieval before materialization
shared_rls.foreign_lookup: id resolution and policy predicate application happen before any row data is materialized; hit and miss follow the identical deny path

variants.equal_contract: ISO1-ISO8 apply to both variants with zero tolerance; topology alone may not change the contract

hard_invariants.ISO1: the caller never receives content bytes of another scope
hard_invariants.ISO2: a deny/miss response never discloses foreign ids, metadata, counts, ranks, snippets or existence; deny bodies for all equivalence classes are byte-identical to the canonical deny form and within the frozen timing tolerance
hard_invariants.ISO3: a cache hit never bypasses the current scope/policy/revocation check
hard_invariants.ISO4: after the committed invalidation point of a revoke/move/supersede, the old scope receives no further data from the affected object (no stale cache/projection entry is served)
hard_invariants.ISO5: provenance fields and the canonical scope binding survive indexing, projection and retrieval on every disclosed object
hard_invariants.ISO6: bulk, pagination, aggregation and background re-index paths apply the identical policy contract as single reads
hard_invariants.ISO7: a caller-supplied scope never widens the effective scope of the canonical actor
hard_invariants.ISO8: an unknown or malformed scope denies; it never resolves to a default or fallback scope

invariant_severity: any ISO1-ISO8 violation in an accepted fixture run is FAIL regardless of the weighted decision score

timing_probe_contract.purpose: bounded local error/timing observability check of the object-existence oracle (valid foreign id versus nonexistent id)
timing_probe_contract.method: perf_counter_ns wall time around paired interleaved retrieval calls (foreign and control alternate per sample so slow drift affects both arms equally), identical corpus for both arms

tolerance.rule: signal = |median paired difference|; distinguishable iff signal > max(relative * median_control, absolute_floor_ns)

timing_probe_contract.interpretation: a distinguishable signal is a finding that constrains the variant (finding/limitation or FAIL per the frozen rubric); it is never evidence of production exploitability and never a production SLO claim
timing_probe_contract.no_data_policy: insufficient samples or executor interruption yields NO_DATA, which remains a limitation and never becomes a pass
